text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) will accept people who had links with the communist-era security service as candidates for parliament in the September 21 elections, the group's senior official Jerzy Szmajdzinski said.

- Kazimierz Oleksiak, the president of the Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) farming bank, will run for parliament for the co-ruling Polish Peasants' Party (PSL), a source who declined to be named said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- France is pressing the EU Commission to charge Poland for the losses of the EU automotive concerns, which resulted from duty free imports of the Korean Daewoo cars to Poland.

- The general shareholders meeting of the Agros Lowicz vegetable and fruit processing plant has approved a capital increase to 51 million zlotys. After the increase Agros Holding's stake in the company will rise to 62 percent from 55 percent.

- Adapting Poland's agriculture sector to the EU requirements makes up 50 percent of all of the country's problems related the planned access to the EU, the Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski said.

- Poland's finance and economy ministries and the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, have written off a five billion zlotys debt of the Opole power plant in south-western Poland, the finance ministry said.

- The Polish-Korean Sung San ZEM electrical engineering plant has launched operations in Elk, north-eastern Poland, to produce lighting and other electrical equipment for Daewoo's Polonez, Nexia, Lanos, Tico and J-100 models.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Poland's telecommunications ministry will call a tender for local telephone operators to offer services in six provinces. The move is designed to curb the monopolist position of the state-owned firm TPSA on the local telephone market.
- Direct investments by Dutch companies in Poland have already exceeded $1.2 billion making Holland the fifth biggest foreign investor.

- The general shareholders' meeting of the over-the-counter market firm Ceto has dismissed its president Czeslaw Gawlowski after because the company relations with the Securities Commission (KPW), the treasury ministry and brokerage houses have deteriorated.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Kredyt Bank has signed a partnership agreement with Russia's Moscow Joint Stock Commercial Bank Vozrozhdenyie in Moscow.
ZYCIE
- Poland's treasury ministry has dismissed Alfred Nowak from the post of the Ruch press distribution chain's president.
PARKIET
- The U.S. Merrill Lynch investment bank has recommended buying the Victoria and Fortuna National Investment Funds (NFI) stressing the funds' good growth perspectives.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
